## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Desanāhāravibhaṅga* ("Conveying a Teaching: Analysis") is the fourth section of the *Netti* (Nettippakaraṇa) [SuttaCentral]. It constitutes the detailed analysis (*vibhaṅga*) of the *desanāhāra*, the first of the sixteen modes of conveying (*hāranaya*) that provide an analytical methodology facilitating knowledge and doctrinal scrutiny [Khemananda 1993]. In this hermeneutical method, the exposition elaborates the meaning of a discourse through categories such as gratification, disadvantages, emancipation, fruit, means, and injunction; under this rule, even if only one such category is explicitly formulated in a discourse, the rest are to be supplied [Khemananda 1993].
DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse for the section, registering 694 matching passages across 59 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. In addition to extensive overlap with its commentarial tradition—the *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and *Nettivibhāvinī*—it shares substantial text segments with canonical suttas and treatises, including the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56), the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), the *Kāmasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 1), the *Saccavibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 141), the *Vinaya Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2), the *Kāma Sutta* (Snp 4.1), and the *Paṭisambhidākathā* (Ps 2.6) [DharmaNexus]. Curated cross-references on SuttaCentral confirm these thematic links to texts such as the *Dhammacakkappavattanasutta* (SN 56.11), the *Paṭisambhidākathā* (Ps 2.6, Ps 2.7), and Vinaya ordination narratives [SuttaCentral]. Cross-linguistically, DharmaNexus automatically aligns segments of Ne 4 with Tibetan Buddhist treatises, including the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D4094, 16 matches) and the *Paryāyasaṃgrahaṇī* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* (D4041, 5 matches) [DharmaNexus], while SuttaCentral lists corresponding parallels and citations in northern texts including the Tibetan *Dharma-cakra-pravartana-sūtra* (D 31) and Chinese Vinaya and Āgama accounts (T 109, T 1450) [SuttaCentral].
